answer: A random raven audit then challenges a sample of agents to prove live control, and any failure severs the thread and forfeits the bond. Each agent must stake a bonded identity whose history forms a single unbroken thread, anchored to a verified hardware root; spinning up many identities means paying that bond repeatedly plus attestation fees, so sock-puppet farms bleed capital fast. Reputation also climbs a vine: only sustained, peer-attested work thickens it, so fresh clones start thin and cannot borrow trust. Attack cost scales linearly with fake identities while honest payoff compounds. ...
